DEC_CARD_VERDICTS.alternatives: the seven buttons of the clickable prototype (approve, rephrase, more details, delete, freeze, reject, note) and 1–5 stars.
DEC_CARD_VERDICTS.reason: Seen in the prototype: seven three-line buttons were too big; what should change about a text is said better in the comment than with rephrase or more-details buttons; a note is just a comment without verdict; quality needs a clear scale with keys.
DEC_CARD_VERDICTS.title: The feedback card has four verdicts – approve, reject, approve & freeze, delete – plus a comment; a comment alone is a note; quality is rated with 0–5 stars

DEC_CLIENT_PACKAGE.alternatives: every host adapter talking to the engine on its own.
DEC_CLIENT_PACKAGE.reason: monsterbrain and VS Code need the same engine handling; only the adapter that puts the results into the host's UI differs.
DEC_CLIENT_PACKAGE.title: One TypeScript client for all hosts finds, starts and checks the engine and calls its API

DEC_CLI_MASTER.alternatives: a web app as the core.
DEC_CLI_MASTER.reason: One logic for all front ends; agents and integrations use the same commands and JSON.
DEC_CLI_MASTER.title: The CLI is the master, with an openly documented file format

DEC_DANWOS_TOKENS.reason: Recognition across all danwos tools; the deciwa monster colours are only for pictures.
DEC_DANWOS_TOKENS.title: deciwa uses the danwos colours and tokens

DEC_DATA_ADAPTERS.alternatives: id fields to name array items (data-dependent); special views for `needs.json` or tokens; review by line only.
DEC_DATA_ADAPTERS.reason: Data files – design tokens, configs, `needs.json`, exports – are results too. Every value is an element, leaves included: the document, every object member and every array item. Selectors are JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) with the index for array items; there are no rules that depend on the data (no id fields, no special views for known files). An item that moves when something is inserted in front keeps its review because the engine follows moved elements, for every format. Only standard JSON (no JSON Lines, no JSONC) and the first document of a YAML file.
DEC_DATA_ADAPTERS.title: JSON and YAML files are reviewed value by value; selectors are JSON Pointers

DEC_DECISION_IS_APPROVAL.alternatives: separate decision records in the source.
DEC_DECISION_IS_APPROVAL.reason: Decisions can then be mapped onto anything that is an element.
DEC_DECISION_IS_APPROVAL.title: A decision is an approved statement, not an extra object

DEC_DECIWA_FOLDER.alternatives: sidecar files next to each source.
DEC_DECIWA_FOLDER.reason: The files must not get in the user's way; a parent folder covers several repositories or repositories that must stay untouched.
DEC_DECIWA_FOLDER.title: All deciwa files in one .deciwa/ folder at the repository root or in a parent folder

DEC_DOCS_IN_REPO.alternatives: decisions in Daniel's knowledge base only; MkDocs Material (plain text without ids or traceability).
DEC_DOCS_IN_REPO.reason: Others develop in the repository too, and decisions act as requirements; Sphinx-Needs gives every decision an id, a status and links, and deciwa can later review its own docs.
DEC_DOCS_IN_REPO.title: Decisions, features and concepts live in the repository as Sphinx docs with Sphinx-Needs

DEC_FACT_BLOCKS.alternatives: a whole section as one fact (fewer, coarser approvals); explicit markup with an id per fact; facts extracted by AI.
DEC_FACT_BLOCKS.reason: The selectors and fingerprints of the Markdown adapter make every block reviewable without markup, the same on every run; an AI that finds the facts by meaning cuts differently each time and approvals lose their anchor. The brain is written in bullets and tables already, with one fact per list item as the writing rule. A facts file can also be approved as a whole; that approval gets stale on any change in the file, while the approvals of its facts stay per fact.
DEC_FACT_BLOCKS.title: A fact is a structural block of a facts file – a list item, a table row or a free paragraph – not a meaning found in the text

DEC_FEEDBACK_CARD.title: Feedback card at the element is the default UI; side panel is the alternative; radial menu dropped

DEC_FORMATS.reason: Docs-as-code plus the results and code around it.
DEC_FORMATS.title: Formats: text, HTML, Python, C, JS, TS, rST, Markdown, AsciiDoc

DEC_FREEZE.reason: Some wording must survive every edit; the AI must never change it, and deciwa raises an alarm if it changes anyway.
DEC_FREEZE.title: New verdict freeze

DEC_FREEZE_BY_VERDICT.alternatives: an explicit unfreeze command for humans only; deleting the freeze annotation.
DEC_FREEZE_BY_VERDICT.reason: Approving an element again replaces one's own freeze anyway (latest verdict wins while the element is unchanged); a second way to lift it only confuses.
DEC_FREEZE_BY_VERDICT.title: A freeze ends with a new verdict; there is no separate "lift freeze"

DEC_GIT_COMMITTED.reason: Reviews are versioned together with the content.
DEC_GIT_COMMITTED.title: .deciwa/ is committed to Git by default

DEC_HOST_ELEMENTS.alternatives: a DOM scan of the host's rendering (other selectors than the CLI); the host sending its own element list.
DEC_HOST_ELEMENTS.reason: The host renders, the adapter knows the elements – feedback gets the same selectors as in the CLI, so `deciwa todo` points at the source line. Rendered HTML files keep the DOM scan with the file path as source.
DEC_HOST_ELEMENTS.title: In a host the overlay gets its elements from the engine's adapter, matched to the blocks the host marks with their source line

DEC_HOST_EXTENSIONS.alternatives: copying the overlay and a port of the engine into the host; a deciwa integration built into the host.
DEC_HOST_EXTENSIONS.reason: deciwa is developed here only; a host such as monsterbrain or VS Code must not carry a copy of deciwa code. The same server API and overlay serve every host, only a thin adapter differs.
DEC_HOST_EXTENSIONS.title: Host apps get deciwa as an extension that lives in this repository; the host only offers generic extension points

DEC_HOST_ORDER.reason: Daniel uses monsterbrain daily on his knowledge base, the first use of deciwa; it tests the API server, the host element source and the client that VS Code needs later.
DEC_HOST_ORDER.title: monsterbrain is the first host, before VS Code

DEC_HOVER_SELECT.alternatives: line-based selection like a code review.
DEC_HOVER_SELECT.reason: Pointing must be as fast as looking.
DEC_HOVER_SELECT.title: Format objects are highlighted on hover and directly selectable; free text selection down to single words

DEC_HTML_ADAPTER.alternatives: the DOM scan of the rendered page only (no source lines, no review of the code).
DEC_HTML_ADAPTER.reason: HTML results in a knowledge base are reviewed both as a page and as code; with source lines from the engine, feedback on the page points at the source and `deciwa todo` names the line. It follows the rules of the browser's DOM scan, so the selectors stay the same.
DEC_HTML_ADAPTER.title: HTML files are read by an adapter in the engine, with source lines; the rendered page and the source view share its elements

DEC_INTEGRATIONS.reason: Reviews happen where people already work – editor, browser, chat; the desktop app covers people without an IDE.
DEC_INTEGRATIONS.title: Integrations: VS Code, Chrome, Claude UI, desktop app

DEC_NO_ENFORCING.reason: Enforcing decisions is not possible; doing the work is the job of the AI or the developer.
DEC_NO_ENFORCING.title: deciwa collects, evaluates and shows; it does not watch that decisions are kept

DEC_NO_MARKERS.alternatives: [CHECK]-style markers or ids in the text.
DEC_NO_MARKERS.reason: The source stays clean and every element stays documented (a Sphinx-Needs requirement, a heading, a Python function, an HTML container, a selected word).
DEC_NO_MARKERS.title: No markers in the source; elements come from the content

DEC_PACKAGES.alternatives: one package with everything (the first prototype, deciwa_proto).
DEC_PACKAGES.reason: The CLI and the server are reused by every integration; the logic stays in one place (core); integrations such as Sphinx, VS Code or Chrome stay independent of each other.
DEC_PACKAGES.title: deciwa is one repository of separate packages: core, server, CLI, UI and one per integration

DEC_PURPOSE.alternatives: a decision log only; a tool for one group (developers, AI agents or management).
DEC_PURPOSE.reason: Daniel needs a simple way to review content and agree to statements (trigger: his own work in his knowledge base).
DEC_PURPOSE.title: deciwa is a review and decision tool for everyone who works with docs and code

DEC_PYTHON_ADAPTER.alternatives: tree-sitter for all languages at once (more dependencies, a bigger standalone engine); review of single lines only.
DEC_PYTHON_ADAPTER.reason: Code repositories are reviewed in monsterbrain next to the knowledge base; ast gives exact line ranges without a new dependency. The Python adapter moves up from 0.4; JS, TS and C follow with tree-sitter.
DEC_PYTHON_ADAPTER.title: Python source is reviewed per class, function, method and statement outside functions, read with the standard library ast

DEC_REPLACES_CHECK.reason: A question at the element with addressee and state replaces a marker in the text ({need}`DEC_NO_MARKERS`); open questions show up in every integration instead of being searched with `rg`.
DEC_REPLACES_CHECK.title: deciwa replaces the [CHECK] markers in Daniel's knowledge base

DEC_REVIEW_ON_RESULTS.reason: Rendered docs and websites are what reviewers see; deciwa must not look like a pull-request code review. The source view shows the same element.
DEC_REVIEW_ON_RESULTS.title: Reviews happen on results, not only on source

DEC_SERVE_API_ONLY.alternatives: the full `deciwa serve` with a built site; the engine as a Python library inside the host.
DEC_SERVE_API_ONLY.reason: A host renders the content itself and only needs the engine's logic; port 0 and a token keep several hosts and other local pages apart; closing stdin ends the engine, so it never outlives its host.
DEC_SERVE_API_ONLY.title: A host talks to deciwa serve --api-only: the JSON API for one folder, no build, token and handshake, stops with the host

DEC_SKILLS.reason: Agents should pick up feedback and ask questions without extra prompting (deciwa-work, deciwa-ask).
DEC_SKILLS.title: One or two agent skills for working with deciwa

DEC_STANDALONE_ENGINE.alternatives: Python and `uv tool install deciwa` as a prerequisite for every host; a TypeScript port of the core.
DEC_STANDALONE_ENGINE.reason: monsterbrain will be distributed and the VS Code extension must work without Python on the machine; users install one app, not a Python environment.
DEC_STANDALONE_ENGINE.title: The Python parts can be shipped as a standalone binary that host apps bundle

DEC_THREE_MODES.alternatives: stars as part of a verdict.
DEC_THREE_MODES.reason: Stars are a quick judgement independent of any verdict, to focus on weak areas later; AI questions are answered at the element by verdict or text.
DEC_THREE_MODES.title: Three ways of working that stay separate: feedback, quality rating, AI communication

DEC_VERDICTS.reason: Approve, reject, note and the quick actions rephrase, more details and delete give the AI a complete instruction with one click.
DEC_VERDICTS.title: Feedback verdicts plus quick actions for the AI

DEC_WEB_HOSTING.reason: The docs workflow already publishes deciwa.danwos.dev; versioned paths allow pinning.
DEC_WEB_HOSTING.title: The web script is hosted with the docs under deciwa.danwos.dev/js/<version>/

DEC_WEB_ONE_LINE.alternatives: `?deciwa` in the address as the only way to load it.
DEC_WEB_ONE_LINE.reason: Quick integration and tests without prior knowledge; every setting is optional, hiding deciwa behind `?deciwa` is an opt-in.
DEC_WEB_ONE_LINE.title: One script tag is enough – deciwa always appears where it is loaded

DEC_WEB_SCRIPT_FIRST.alternatives: the web script as part of the Chrome extension in 0.3.
DEC_WEB_SCRIPT_FIRST.reason: The first real use is the danwos website; the Chrome extension builds on the same script.
DEC_WEB_SCRIPT_FIRST.title: The web script comes as 0.2, before VS Code

DEC_WEB_SOURCE.alternatives: a required `deciwa-source` meta tag on every page.
DEC_WEB_SOURCE.reason: deciwa must work without a configuration file; a mapping added later must not lose feedback.
DEC_WEB_SOURCE.title: Mapping pages to source files is optional; the address is the fallback

PROP_ADAPTER_API.title: One small adapter interface for all formats

PROP_CLI_CHECK.content:
`deciwa status --fail-on frozen-changed,orphaned` exits with `3` when such
elements exist. deciwa still only shows – the team decides whether CI stops.
Optional for 0.1.
PROP_CLI_CHECK.title: deciwa status can fail a CI run on freeze alarms

PROP_CLI_JSON.content:
`--json` prints `{"deciwa": "0.1", "command": "<name>", "ok": true,
"result": …}`; errors print `"ok": false` with an `error` object
(`code`, `message`). Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` error, `2` usage error. Human
output may change between versions; the JSON envelope may not.
PROP_CLI_JSON.title: JSON output has one envelope for every command

PROP_DOCS_REVIEW_SOURCE.content:
A translation is checked like any wording, but the binding statement is
the English one: `.deciwa/` only holds reviews of the English pages. The
German pages carry the overlay only as the offline demo for visitors.
PROP_DOCS_REVIEW_SOURCE.title: Reviews and decisions happen only on the English docs

PROP_DOCS_TRANSLATION.content:
Everybody writes and changes the English Markdown. The translations live in
`docs/locales/<language>/LC_MESSAGES/*.po`, one catalog per page plus
`needs.po` for the titles and fields of needs. When an English paragraph
changes, its translation becomes `fuzzy` and the old one stays visible
until somebody updates it. English is published at the root, German in
`de/`; a switcher in the sidebar leads to the same page in the other
language.
PROP_DOCS_TRANSLATION.title: English is the source of the docs; German is a translation in gettext catalogs

PROP_DOM_ADAPTER.content:
A small adapter in JavaScript reads the DOM of the review root and returns
the same element list as the other adapters:

- sections from the heading outline `h1`–`h6` (web pages rarely nest real
  `<section>` elements), named by their heading path,
- paragraphs, list items, table rows (`tr` outside `thead`), code blocks
  (`pre`), notes (`aside`, `[role=note]`), pictures (`img`, `svg`,
  `figure`, `picture`) – counted per section as in Markdown,
- left out: `nav`, `header`, `footer`, `form`, `[hidden]`, `[aria-hidden=true]`,
  `script`, `style` and everything matching `data-ignore`.

The fingerprint is SHA-256 over the normalised text, computed with
`crypto.subtle` – the same value as `model.fingerprint` in Python, so the CLI
and the browser agree on stale elements. The offline overlay switches from
its local FNV hash to this one. Pictures are fingerprinted by `src`, `alt`
and caption.

Pages with build hints (`#deciwa-page`, as the Sphinx extension writes it)
skip the scan and use the hints.
PROP_DOM_ADAPTER.title: The web script finds the elements of a rendered page itself

PROP_ENGINE_BINARY.content:
- **Content:** `deciwa-core`, `-server`, `-cli` and the overlay files of
  `deciwa-ui`. Not `deciwa-sphinx`: Sphinx builds keep running in the docs
  project's own Python environment.
- **Form:** PyInstaller *one-folder* (starts fast; *one-file* unpacks on every
  start), so the host can sign every file inside.
- **Platforms:** linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos-arm64, macos-x64, windows-x64 –
  built in GitHub Actions on each platform, smoke-tested with
  `deciwa --version` and `serve --api-only` against a test folder.
- **Release:** a zip per platform in the releases of `danwos/deciwa`. A host
  pins an engine version and fetches it at its own build time; it never
  downloads code at run time.
- **Signing:** the host signs the bundled engine together with its own code
  (Apple notarisation requires every binary inside the app to be signed).
- **Size:** expected 20–40 MB per platform; to be measured with the first
  build.
sections: Host apps and the standalone engine
PROP_ENGINE_BINARY.title: The engine is built with PyInstaller, one folder per platform

PROP_FILE_LAYOUT.content:
The path under `annotations/` mirrors the source path relative to the folder
that holds `.deciwa/`. The CLI writes sorted keys, two-space indent, one
annotation after the other by creation time and a final newline – so Git
diffs stay small and merge conflicts stay rare.
PROP_FILE_LAYOUT.title: One annotation file per source, deterministic JSON

PROP_FINGERPRINT.content:
`sha256` over the element's source text after Unicode NFC, trimming and
collapsing runs of whitespace into one space. Markup stays in: turning a word
bold makes an approval `stale`.
PROP_FINGERPRINT.title: The fingerprint covers the source text with whitespace normalised

PROP_FREE_TEXT.content:
Selecting a word stores the structural selector of the element that contains
it plus a `TextQuoteSelector` (exact, prefix, suffix) and a
`TextPositionSelector` relative to that element. This works in every format,
and the fingerprint covers only the selected text.
PROP_FREE_TEXT.title: A free text selection is a text quote inside its nearest element

PROP_LATEST_WINS.content:
A misclick or a second thought must not pile up entries. As long as the
element's fingerprint is the same, a new verdict of the same author replaces
the old verdict, and a new rating the old rating. Once the element changed,
earlier annotations stay as history (that is how `stale` works). Notes and
questions are never replaced; a comment that came with a replaced verdict is
kept as a note. That is also how a freeze ends: the author gives another verdict
({need}`DEC_FREEZE_BY_VERDICT`).
PROP_LATEST_WINS.title: While an element is unchanged, an author's latest verdict and latest rating replace the earlier ones

PROP_LAYERS.content:
Inside `deciwa.core`:

| Module | Contains | May use |
|---|---|---|
| `deciwa.core.model` | annotations, ids, fingerprints, schema version | – |
| `deciwa.core.adapters` (0.1) | one module per format; text in, elements out | model |
| `deciwa.core.store` | finding `.deciwa/`, reading and writing annotation files, config | model |
| `deciwa.core.engine` | resolving selectors, states, review rules, todo lists, export/import | model, adapters, store |

Every other package is a front end and uses only `deciwa.core.Project`
(never the store or the files directly), so the hosted service can later
replace `store` without changing them.
PROP_LAYERS.title: The core is split into layers with a strict dependency direction

PROP_OVERLAY_PARTS.content:
| Part | Variants |
|---|---|
| element source | Sphinx (`#deciwa-page` from the build) · DOM scan (the HTML adapter below) |
| store | `deciwa serve` · offline in the browser · a remote deciwa server (later) |
| UI | card, panel, bars, guided review – unchanged |

The parts meet in small interfaces: an element source returns the element
list of the page, a store answers the calls the overlay makes today
(`/api/page`, `/api/annotate`, …). The Sphinx integration keeps working
unchanged and is the test that the split did not break anything.
PROP_OVERLAY_PARTS.title: The overlay is split into element source, store and UI

PROP_PYTHON_CORE.content:
rST with Sphinx-Needs is an MVP format, and only docutils parses rST fully.
The same code then runs inside a Sphinx build to tag the rendered HTML with
selectors – the base for review on results. The TypeScript integrations of
0.3/0.4 talk to the CLI through `--json` and `deciwa serve`, as
{need}`DEC_CLI_MASTER` demands anyway. If the browser ever needs element
finding without a local CLI, a WASM or TypeScript port of single adapters
stays possible because the selectors are a documented format.
PROP_PYTHON_CORE.title: The core and the CLI are written in Python

PROP_RESOLVE.content:
1. **Structural** – the adapter's element list has an element with exactly
   this selector.
2. **Text quote** – the exact text occurs once in the file; if it occurs
   several times, prefix and suffix decide. Whitespace differences are
   ignored.
3. **Position** – only if the text at that position still matches the
   fingerprint.

If the selector that hit is not the first one, the engine reports a
`relinked` hint so `deciwa` can update the stored selectors (only on an
explicit `deciwa relink`, never silently). Nothing hits → `orphaned`.
Text quote and position follow the
[W3C Web Annotation Data Model](https://www.w3.org/TR/annotation-model/).
PROP_RESOLVE.title: Selectors are tried in a fixed order and the first unique hit wins

PROP_ROLLOUT_LOCATION.content:
`deciwa init` in the root. Archive and source folders go into
`[ignore]`, because they are never reviewed.
PROP_ROLLOUT_LOCATION.title: .deciwa/ at the root of the knowledge base, committed

PROP_ROLLOUT_MIGRATE.content:
A one-off script finds every `[CHECK]` line, creates a `request` on the
element that contains it (question and addressee from the marker text) and
removes the marker from the text. After that, agents use `deciwa-ask`
instead of writing markers.
PROP_ROLLOUT_MIGRATE.title: Existing [CHECK] markers are migrated once into requests

PROP_RST_DOCUTILS.content:
docutils keeps source lines on every node. Unknown directives and roles
(Sphinx, Sphinx-Needs, any extension) are registered as generic
placeholders, so a file parses without `conf.py` and without importing
extensions. Need directives are recognised by name; their `:id:` gives the
`sphinx-needs:` selector.
PROP_RST_DOCUTILS.title: The rST adapter parses with docutils, without running Sphinx

PROP_SCHEMA.content:
`schema/deciwa-0.1.schema.json` is published with the CLI and in these docs.
The CLI validates every file it reads. A new major field means a new schema
version; the CLI reads older versions and writes the newest.
PROP_SCHEMA.title: A JSON Schema is the documented contract

PROP_SELECTORS.content:
Heading paths survive moves of whole sections and edits in other sections.
The counter (`#2`) breaks when a paragraph is inserted above – that is why
every annotation also stores a text quote ({doc}`file-format`), which the
engine tries next. Duplicate heading names in one path get a suffix
(`Notes~2`).
PROP_SELECTORS.title: Element selectors are paths of headings plus a per-section counter

PROP_SKILLS_FORMAT.content:
`skills/deciwa-work/SKILL.md` and `skills/deciwa-ask/SKILL.md`, each a short
instruction plus the CLI calls it uses. The skills only call the CLI with
`--json` – never the files – and sign as `agent:<name>`.
PROP_SKILLS_FORMAT.title: Two skills in the Agent Skills format, shipped in the repository

PROP_SNAPSHOT.content:
Without it deciwa can tell *that* an approved or frozen text changed, but not
*what* it looked like – and the freeze alarm must show the old wording
({need}`DEC_FREEZE`). The cost is some duplicate text in `.deciwa/`.
PROP_SNAPSHOT.title: The snapshot of the element text is stored with every annotation

PROP_STATE_RULES.content:
An open request is shown as a badge on top of every other state, so
`approved` with an open question is still visible as approved. A resolved
quick action does not approve anything: after `deciwa resolve` the element
falls back to its previous state, and the `stale` check shows that it was
changed.
PROP_STATE_RULES.title: State rules in this order

PROP_TOOLING.content:
- **uv** for environments, locking and `uv tool install deciwa`.
- **ruff** for lint and format, **pytest** for tests, **mypy** strict for
  `src/deciwa/model` and `src/deciwa/engine`.
- **click** for the CLI – small, stable, no magic.
- **pydantic** is not used; the model is plain dataclasses plus a JSON
  Schema in `schema/` so other languages can validate the files too.
- Runtime dependencies for 0.1: `click`, `markdown-it-py`, `docutils`,
  `pyyaml` (frontmatter). Sphinx only as an optional extra
  (`deciwa[sphinx]`).
PROP_TOOLING.title: Tooling: Python 3.12+, uv, ruff, pytest, click

PROP_VSCODE_PLATFORM.content:
`vsce package --target <platform>` builds one extension package per platform,
each with its engine. A universal package without engine uses `deciwa` on
`PATH` – for platforms without a build.
sections: Host apps and the standalone engine
PROP_VSCODE_PLATFORM.title: VS Code ships one package per platform with the engine inside

PROP_WEB_BUNDLE.content:
The overlay sources become ES modules in `packages/ui/js/`. esbuild (no
framework) builds two files:

- `deciwa-overlay.js` – for the Python package and the Sphinx extension, as today,
- `deciwa.js` – the web script: one file with the CSS and the deciwa picture
  inlined.

On foreign pages the UI lives in a Shadow DOM, so the page's CSS cannot break
the overlay and the overlay's CSS cannot change the page.
PROP_WEB_BUNDLE.title: One bundle built with esbuild, the UI inside a Shadow DOM

PROP_WEB_FILES.content:
A page reviewed with the web script whose source is the fallback
`web:<host><path>` is stored as `annotations/_web/<host>/<path>.json`; the
path `/` becomes `index`, a port is written as `_<port>`, and the file keeps
the address in its `source` field. `deciwa import` applies the rules of
`[web]` first: a rule only counts when its file exists, so mapped pages land
in the file of their source and everything else keeps its address. When a
rule is added later, `deciwa remap` moves the annotations of `_web/` to
their source files.

An export from the web script carries the elements of its pages (selector,
kind, label, text, fingerprint). The import keeps them in
`.deciwa/web-pages.json` by address, so `todo`, `show` and `status` work
without parsing HTML in Python; the selectors stay `html:…`, also for pages
mapped to a Markdown file. Such an import replaces only the review data of
the pages in the file, never the rest of the project.
PROP_WEB_FILES.title: Web pages without a source file are stored under their address

PROP_WEB_HOSTING.content:
The docs workflow publishes `deciwa.js` to `https://deciwa.danwos.dev/js/<release>/deciwa.js`,
where the release is major and minor of `packages/ui/package.json` (`0.2`);
`/js/latest/deciwa.js` follows the newest release. During the prototype
phase every deploy overwrites the one published release – the release
number is not raised yet. Once releases are raised, the builds of earlier
releases are kept, so a published release never changes and sites can pin
it with a Subresource Integrity hash.
Decided: {need}`DEC_WEB_HOSTING`.
PROP_WEB_HOSTING.title: The web script is hosted with the docs under a versioned path

PROP_WEB_INDEX.content:
Without a build there is no `elements.json`. The web script stores the
element list of each page it has seen (selector, kind, label, text,
fingerprint) in the browser, so the project panel lists all visited pages
and stale elements are found when a page is opened again. An export carries
this index along, so the CLI can resolve web annotations without an HTML
adapter in Python. Reading `sitemap.xml` to list all pages up front can come
later.
PROP_WEB_INDEX.title: The browser remembers the elements of every visited page

PROP_WEB_ONE_LINE.content:
A single `<script src=".../deciwa.js" defer>` without attributes shows the
deciwa button on every page and works offline in the browser. No
configuration file, no build step, no page mapping is needed to try it.
Everything else is an optional attribute ({doc}`../integrations/web`).
Decided: {need}`DEC_WEB_ONE_LINE`.
`data-activate="param"` is an opt-in for public sites: deciwa then loads
only when the address contains `?deciwa`.
PROP_WEB_ONE_LINE.title: Loading the script is enough – deciwa always appears

PROP_WEB_RESCAN.content:
The script scans again after client-side navigation (`popstate`,
`astro:page-load`, `turbo:load`) and, throttled, when a `MutationObserver`
sees changes inside the review root. Open cards stay attached to their
element through its selector.
PROP_WEB_RESCAN.title: Pages that change after loading are scanned again

PROP_WEB_SOURCE.content:
The source of a page is, in this order:

1. `<meta name="deciwa-source" content="…">` on the page,
2. the first matching rule of `[web].sources` in `.deciwa/config.toml`
   (applied by the CLI on import, see {doc}`file-format`),
3. the fallback, which always works: `web:<host><path>`, e.g.
   `web:danwos.dev/services/`. Query and fragment are dropped, `index.html`
   and a missing trailing slash count as the same page.

The browser always stores the address; a mapping added later moves the
annotations to the source file without losing any.
Decided: {need}`DEC_WEB_SOURCE`.
PROP_WEB_SOURCE.title: A page is identified by its meta tag, a mapping rule or its address

Q_ASSUMPTION.content:
`[ASSUMPTION]` says "this number has no evidence". It could become a
request, or stay as a marker because it must also be visible to readers of
a PDF or slide built from the text.
Q_ASSUMPTION.title: Does [ASSUMPTION] become a request too?

Q_CORE_LANG.content:
Yes → PROP_PYTHON_CORE and PROP_TOOLING become decisions. No → which
language, and how should the rST/Sphinx-Needs adapter work?
Q_CORE_LANG.title: Python for the core and the CLI?

Q_ENGINE_BINARY_TOOL.content:
Proposal: PyInstaller – widely used, simple, no C compiler. Alternatives:
Nuitka (compiles to C: faster and smaller, but long builds and a C compiler
per platform); python-build-standalone plus the installed packages (no
freezing problems, but bigger and many loose files).
sections: Host apps and the standalone engine
Q_ENGINE_BINARY_TOOL.title: Which tool builds the standalone engine?

Q_FINGERPRINT_MARKUP.content:
With markup in the fingerprint, bold, a new link or a re-wrapped table makes
an approved statement `stale`. Without it, only changes to the words do – but
deciwa then has to strip markup per format. Proposal: keep markup in for 0.1
(simple, safe); revisit if it is too noisy in the knowledge base.
Q_FINGERPRINT_MARKUP.title: Should pure formatting changes make an approval stale?

Q_MARKERS.content:
Answered by Daniel (2026-10-22): deciwa replaces `[CHECK]` – see
{need}`DEC_REPLACES_CHECK`. `[ASSUMPTION]` is still open:
{need}`Q_ASSUMPTION`.
Q_MARKERS.title: Does deciwa replace [CHECK] and [ASSUMPTION], or only [CHECK]?

Q_NEED_TYPES.content:
Proposal: read them from `needs.json` if the project builds one, otherwise
from `.deciwa/config.toml` (`needs.directives = ["req", "spec", ...]`), and
fall back to the Sphinx-Needs defaults (`req`, `spec`, `impl`, `test`,
`need`). OK, or should deciwa read `conf.py` / `ubproject.toml` directly?
Q_NEED_TYPES.title: Which directive names count as needs?

Q_OVERLAY_LANGUAGE.content:
Today every label of the overlay is English. It could take its language
from `<html lang>` and ship a small dictionary per language.
Q_OVERLAY_LANGUAGE.title: Should the overlay speak German on German pages?

Q_QUICK_ACTIONS.content:
Rephrase and more details are now said in the comment ({need}`DEC_CARD_VERDICTS`).
Candidates for extra one-click jobs: shorten, split, add source, translate.
None, a fixed set, or configurable in `.deciwa/config.toml`?
Q_QUICK_ACTIONS.title: Are there quick actions besides delete?

Q_REVIEW_UI_01.content:
VS Code comes in 0.3. In 0.1 reviewing happens through the CLI and through
Claude ("go through this file with me", using the skills). Options: (a) that
is enough for 0.1; (b) pull a minimal HTML overlay into 0.1, built from the
clickable prototype and served by a first `deciwa serve`.
Q_REVIEW_UI_01.title: How does Daniel review in 0.1 without an editor integration?

Q_SKILL_INSTALL.content:
Options: (a) `deciwa skills install` copies them into `.claude/skills/` of the
current project; (b) a Claude Code plugin that bundles both skills; (c) both.
Proposal: (a) for 0.1, (b) once the CLI is published.
Q_SKILL_INSTALL.title: How do the skills get into a project?

Q_UNFREEZE.content:
Options were: (a) a new verdict on the element ends the freeze; (b) an
explicit `deciwa unfreeze <id>`; (c) only by deleting the freeze annotation.
Answered by Daniel (2026-10-19): (a) – see {need}`DEC_FREEZE_BY_VERDICT`.
Q_UNFREEZE.title: How is a freeze lifted?

Q_WEB_STEP.content:
Proposal was: right after the prototype, before VS Code – the first real use
is the danwos website, and the Chrome extension builds on it.
Answered by Daniel (2026-10-20): yes, as 0.2 – see {need}`DEC_WEB_SCRIPT_FIRST`.
Q_WEB_STEP.title: When does the web script come?

alternatives.description: options that were considered and not taken

arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

constraints.description: List of constraint names, which are defined for this need.

constraints_error.description: An error message set if any constraint failed, and `error_message` field is set in config.

constraints_passed.description: True if all constraints passed, False if any failed, None if not yet checked.

constraints_results.description: Mapping of constraint name, to check name, to result, None if not yet checked.

content.description: The main content of the need.

docname.description: Name of the document where the need is defined (None if external).

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_import.description: If true, the need was derived from an import.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

post_template.description: The template key, if the post_content was created from a jinja template.

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

reason.description: why it was decided this way

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.

to.description: who has to answer a question
